algorithm: Each case runs a seeded stub model with latency timing, correctness is exact-match, and an LLM-as-judge rubric scores the output text.
complexity: O(N) over N test cases; each case is one stub call plus rubric checks.
data_flow_ascii:
test cases -> run_case (stub model + latency + exact match) -> results
results + rubric -> judge_score per case -> judged scores
results + judged -> summarize -> accuracy, latency, judge averages
description_sentence: An evaluation harness that runs test cases against a stub model, measures accuracy and latency, and adds an LLM-as-judge rubric score per case.
failure_note: A stub model crash is caught per case and recorded as incorrect with the error text, so one bad case never kills the run.

functions.desc: Seeded arithmetic test cases with expected answers.
functions.name: build_cases

functions.desc: Deterministic stub model: usually right, sometimes off by one.
functions.name: stub_model

functions.desc: Run one case: model output, latency, exact-match correctness.
functions.name: run_case
functions.signature: run_case(case: dict, model_fn, seed: int) -> dict

functions.desc: LLM-as-judge sim: rubric checks over the output text, 0..1.
functions.name: judge_score

functions.desc: Aggregate accuracy, avg/p95 latency, and average judge score.
functions.name: summarize

functions.desc: Seeded demo: run cases, judge them, print the table and summary.
functions.name: run_demo

functions.desc: Build the command-line parser for the demo.
functions.name: build_parser

functions.desc: Entry point: seeded eval harness demo.
functions.name: main

label: eval_harness
output_shape: Prints a per-case table (input, expected, output, correct, latency, judge score) and a summary line with accuracy and latency stats.
pitch_sentence: I built a {topic} that grades model answers for accuracy and latency and adds an LLM-as-judge rubric score per case.

qa.a: A deterministic stub: correct unless a hash of the case id hits the 25 percent bucket, where it answers off by one.
qa.q: What does the stub model do?

qa.a: It simulates rubric grading with keyword checks and a length penalty, giving a second quality signal beyond exact match.
Swap stub_model for a real model call; run_case, judge_score, and summarize are backend-agnostic.
qa.q: Can this evaluate a real model?

resume_bullet_template: Built a {topic} in Python with seeded test cases, latency measurement, and an LLM-as-judge rubric scorer.
run_notes: --cases sets the number of seeded test cases; the judge rubric lives in build_rubric().
scaling_note: Sequential runs suit hundreds of cases; thousands would want parallel workers and a persistent results store.
storage_note: No persistence: cases, results, and summaries are regenerated from the seed each run.
tradeoff_note: Exact-match correctness is strict and reproducible but penalizes correct answers phrased differently; the judge score softens that.
